en: Buddhavamsa 1.
The Chapter on the Jewel-Perambulation.
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
And Brahmā Sahampati, the lord of the world,
with palms joined, entreated the Unsurpassed One:
"There are beings here who have little dust in their eyes."
Desire the Dhamma for the sake of this compassionate people.
[I seek it] from one perfected in true knowledge and conduct,
a Tathāgata, a bearer of radiance, who bears his final body.
Compassion for all beings arose in the Tathāgata, the peerless person: "Indeed, these beings,
including gods and humans, do not know this."
What kind of person is this Buddha, the supreme among men?
What is the nature of his power of supernormal success and his power of wisdom?
And what is the nature of the Buddha’s power for the benefit of the world?
Neither gods nor humans know this:
that this Buddha is such a supreme among men;
that his power of psychic potency and his power of wisdom are such as these.
Such is the power of the Buddha for the welfare of the world.
Come now, I shall demonstrate that unsurpassed power of the Buddha.
“I shall construct a walkway in the sky, adorned with jewels.
Thus spoke the earth-dwelling deities, the Mahārājikas, and the Tāvatiṁsas.
The Yāma gods, the Tusita gods, the Nimmānarati gods,
those who are Paranimmitavasavatti, and the Brahmakāyika gods,
being filled with joy, raised a vast cry.
The earth, together with its devas, was illuminated,
as were the vast, unconfined spaces between worlds;
and the intense darkness was then dispelled.
Having seen this wonderful miracle,
a vast and sublime radiance arose, surpassing that of gods, gandhabbas, humans, and rakkhasas.
In this world and the next,
both together, below, above, and across in all directions—
supreme among beings, peerless, the Leader.
The Teacher, honored by gods and men,
possessed of great majesty and the marks of a hundred merits,
displayed a wondrous miracle.
Thus entreated by the best of gods, the Visionary,
the Supreme among Men, the Leader of the World, having then considered the welfare [of beings], had a walking path constructed.
It was well-constructed and fashioned from every kind of jewel.
The Blessed One possessed mastery over the three miracles: the miracle of psychic power, the miracle of mind-reading, and the miracle of instruction.
The Leader of the World had a walking path measured out,
perfectly constructed and adorned with all kinds of jewels,
throughout the ten-thousandfold world system.
On that supreme mountain Sineru,
he displayed pillars in succession,
as well as walkways made of jewels.
Having traversed ten thousand [leagues],
the Victor had a walking path constructed,
with sides made entirely of gold.
On the walkway made of jewels,
there were rows of scales and golden planks.
The railings were made entirely of gold,
fashioned on both sides,
and strewn with sand of jewels and pearls.
Created and made of jewels,
it illuminates all directions like the risen sun with its hundred rays.
On that walkway, the wise and perfectly enlightened one,
possessing the thirty-two excellent marks,
shone resplendently.
The Victor paced back and forth upon the walkway.
There were divine mandārava flowers,
lotuses, and pārichattaka trees.
All the gods assembled together sprinkle him as he walks back and forth;
the hosts of gods behold him.
The ten thousand worlds were filled with joy;
bowing in homage, they fell prostrate,
thrilled, delighted, and overjoyed.
The gods of the Thirty-three, the Yāma gods,
and the Tusita deities,
as well as the gods who Delight in Creation;
Those gods who possess sovereign power,
with uplifted minds and joyful hearts,
behold the Leader of the World.
Gods, gandhabbas, humans, and rakkhasas,
nāgas, supaṇṇas, and even kinnaras—
all behold you, who are compassionate for the welfare of the world.
Like the orb of the moon risen in the sky:
the Ābhassara, Subhakiṇha,
Vehapphala, and Akaniṭṭha deities.
Clad in perfectly pure white garments,
they stand with palms joined in reverence;
they scatter flowers of five different colors.
Then they scattered mandārava flowers mixed with sandalwood powder and waved their garments in the air, crying out:
"O Jina, you who are compassionate for the welfare of the world!"
You are the Teacher and the banner,
the standard and the sacrificial post for living beings;
you are the ultimate refuge and the firm foundation.
And the Island, the supreme among bipeds.
The deities of the ten-thousandfold world system,
possessed of great psychic power;
Surrounding him, they pay homage,
joyful, elated, and filled with delight—
the deities and the celestial maidens.
With serene and joyful minds,
they worship the Bull among Men with flowers of five colors.
The hosts of gods, seeing him,
were serene and joyful in mind;
with flowers of five colors, they—
They worship the Bull among Men:
"Oh, what a marvel in the world!
A wonder that makes the hair stand on end!"
"Never before has there been such a marvel,
hair-raising and extraordinary," [they said] in their respective abodes.
Having sat down,
the deities laughed a great laugh upon seeing that wonderful marvel in the sky.
Those dwelling in the sky and those dwelling on the earth,
those who live along grassy paths,
all pay homage with palms joined in reverence.
They were joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness—
even those long-lived *nāgas*,
who were meritorious and possessed of great psychic power.
Delighted, they pay homage and worship the Supreme among Men;
they set up musical performances.
In the sky, upon the path of the wind,
they play instruments bound with leather,
seeing this marvel in the heavens.
Cymbals and drums, and many kettledrums as well,
resounded in the sky.
Having seen this marvel in the sky:
"Truly wonderful for us today has arisen this hair-raising phenomenon!"
"We have obtained the permanent accomplishment of our goal;
the opportune moment has been secured for us.
Having heard from them that "the Buddha [is here],"...
Rapture arose at that moment;
saying "Buddha, Buddha," they stood with palms joined in reverence.
The sounds of *hiṅkāra* and cries of "well done," shouts of exultation and cheering,
and various beings in the sky—
They move about with palms joined in reverence. They sing, clap their hands,
play instruments, beat their limbs, and dance.
They release flowers of five colors,
mandārava blossoms mixed with sandalwood powder.
"Just as for you, O Great Hero,"
On his feet are the marks of wheels;
they are adorned with banners,
thunderbolts, flags, and increasing hooks.
Peerless in virtue, concentration,
and wisdom regarding form;
equal to the unequaled in liberation.
At the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma,
ten times the strength of an elephant was your natural physical power.
Peerless in the power of supernormal success in setting the Wheel of Dhamma in motion—
thus endowed with all virtues, [I pay homage to you].
Worship the Great Sage, the compassionate Lord of the World, who is endowed with all noble qualities.
Salutation, praise, homage,
and eulogy; Reverence and worship—
You deserve all of it.
Whatever there may be in the world that is worthy of homage,
you are worthy of that homage.
O Great Hero, most excellent of all,
there is no one equal to you.
Sāriputta is of great wisdom.
Skilled in concentration and jhāna,
even while standing on Vulture Peak,
he beheld the Leader of the World.
Like a fully blossomed king of sal trees,
like the moon in the sky,
or like the sun at midday.
He gazed upon the bull among men,
who was like a blazing lamp-tree or like the newly risen sun.
He beholds the steadfast Leader of the World, resplendent with the radiance of his aura,
amidst five hundred bhikkhus.
He quickly assembled those who had done their duty,
the steadfast ones, whose taints were exhausted and who were stainless.
He displayed a miracle called "Delighting the World";
we too, having gone there, [beheld it].
We shall pay homage to the Jina.
Come, all of us shall go;
we shall question the Jina.
“We shall dispel our doubt after seeing the Leader of the World.
Having agreed, saying “Very well,” they—
Vigilant and with senses restrained,
they took their bowls and robes and approached in haste.
By those whose taints are destroyed, who are stainless,
tamed in the highest taming— by them,
the one of great wisdom, Sāriputta, [was this spoken].
Sāriputta, the great leader of the assembly, approached by means of psychic power, surrounded by those monks.
Sporting like a god in the sky,
he approached by means of psychic power.
He [performed] the clearing of the throat and the hurling.
Maintaining equanimity and firm in their vows,
full of reverence and respect,
they approached the Fully Awakened One.
Having approached, they saw the Self-Existent One, the Leader of the World,
the Wise One risen high into the sky.
Like the moon in the sky,
like a blazing lamp-tree,
and like lightning in the sky.
Just as at midday they behold the sun,
so they behold the Leader of the World—
all five hundred bhikkhus.
They beheld the Leader of the World,
as serene as a lake and like a fully blossomed lotus.
Raising their joined palms,
joyful, elated, and filled with rapture,
they prostrate themselves while paying homage.
At the Teacher’s wheel-mark,
the greatly wise Sāriputta,
who resembles the koraṇḍa flower, [stood].
Skilled in concentration and jhāna,
he pays homage to the Leader of the World,
like a thundering dark cloud.
Resembling a blue lotus,
peerless in the power of his psychic abilities,
Moggallāna possesses great iddhi.
And the elder Mahākassapa too,
resembling molten gold, was ranked foremost among those possessing the ascetic virtues (dhutaguṇa).
Praised by the Teacher,
Anuruddha, the great leader of the community, who is foremost among those with the divine eye.
The chief of kinsmen stood not far from the Blessed One;
regarding what constitutes an offense and what does not, he remained there.
Expert in what is curable,
Upāli was ranked foremost in the Vinaya; he was praised by the Teacher.
One who has penetrated the subtle and refined meaning,
the most excellent teacher among those who discourse, the leader of the assembly,
the son of Mantāṇī, the seer—
Known by the name Puṇṇa—
knowing their minds,
the Sage, skilled in similes, [spoke].
The Great Hero, the Dispeller of Doubt,
spoke of his own virtues:
"Those four incalculable eons..."
The limit of which is not known:
the body of beings, space,
and the infinite world-systems.
The wisdom of the Buddha is immeasurable;
it is not possible for these people to understand it.
What is so wonderful about this in the world?
This miraculous transformation of mine;
many other wonders,
extraordinary, and hair-raising.
When I was in the Tusita realm,
I was then named Santusita;
ten thousand [deities] gathered together, and...
With palms joined, they entreat me:
"It is now the time for you, O Great Hero,
to arise within a mother's womb."
"Delivering the world together with its gods,
awaken to the deathless state!
Having passed away from the Tusita realm,
When he descended into the womb,
the ten-thousandfold world system and the earth trembled at that time.
When I emerged from my mother’s womb fully conscious,
they raised a cry of "Well done! (sādhukāra).
The ten-thousandfold world system shook:
"There is no one equal to my descent,
my birth, or my renunciation."
In the attainment of perfect enlightenment and in the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma, I am supreme; oh,
how wonderful this is in the world!
The greatness of the Buddhas' virtues caused the ten-thousandfold world system to tremble in six ways.
And there was a great radiance,
wonderful and hair-raising.
At that time, the Blessed One—
The Conqueror, the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
displayed himself to the world with its devas and walked back and forth by means of his supernormal power.
While walking back and forth on the cloistered walkway,
the Leader of the World spoke;
he did not turn back in between.
Just as on a four-cubit walking path,
Sāriputta, possessed of great wisdom and skilled in concentration and jhāna, [remained].
Having reached perfection in wisdom,
he asks the Leader of the World:
"O Great Hero, what is your nature?"
O Supreme among Men,
at what time, O Wise One,
was the unsurpassed enlightenment aspired to by you?
What is the nature of generosity, virtue, renunciation,
wisdom, and energy; and of patience, truthfulness, and resolve?
And what are loving-kindness and equanimity like?
O Wise One, Leader of the World, what are the ten perfections like in you?
"How is the perfection of rebirth fulfilled?
And how is the ultimate perfection fulfilled?
Being thus questioned, he explained to him:
With a voice as sweet as the *karavīka* bird,
he brings peace to the heart and causes laughter among the world of gods and men.
Taught by the Conquerors, the Buddhas of the past,
polished and transmitted through the succession of Buddhas,
[it was realized] by means of an intelligence that follows after former existences.
He proclaimed the welfare of the world, including the devas:
“It generates rapture and gladness,
and dispels the sting of sorrow.”
Having held in high esteem the attainment of all success, listen to me:
it is the crushing of intoxication, the dispeller of sorrow.
"Thoroughly practice the path that brings liberation from saṃsāra and the destruction of all suffering."
The section on the Jewel Walkway is finished.
